questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Profuse
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.
Profuse
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Scarce.

Key Points

  • The word "Profuse" means something that is abundant or in great amount. (प्रचुर मात्रा में)
    • Example: She thanked him profusely for his help.
  • "Scarce" refers to something that is in short supply or not easily available. (दुर्लभ)
    • Example: During the drought, food and water were scarce in the region.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Profuse' is 'Scarce'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Scarce.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Humble (विनम्र): Having or showing a modest or low estimate of one's importance.
    • Example: Despite his success, he remains a humble person.
  • Prompt (तत्काल): Done without delay; immediate.
    • Example: She was prompt in answering her emails.
  • Just (न्यायसंगत): Based on or behaving according to what is morally right and fair.
    • Example: The judge gave a just verdict in the case.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Customary
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Customary
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: Option 4.

Key Points

  • The word "Customary" means something that is according to the customs or usual practices; it implies being typical or expected. (रिवाज के अनुसार)
    • Example: It is customary to remove your shoes before entering a temple.
  • "Unusual" refers to something that is not common or typical; it is out of the ordinary. (असामान्य)
    • Example: Her choice of outfit was quite unusual for the formal event.
  • Hence, we can infer that the opposite of 'Customary' is 'Unusual'.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option 4.

Additional Information

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

  • Fashion (फैशन): A popular trend, especially in styles of dress and ornament.
    • Example: She always keeps up with the latest fashion.
  • Protection (सुरक्षा): The action of protecting someone or something.
    • Example: Wearing a helmet provides protection during cycling.
  • Habitual (आदतन): Done or doing constantly or as a habit.
    • Example: He is a habitual latecomer to meetings.

questions.question: Select the correct antonym of the given word. Exodus

For e.g., My daughter promptly awaited the arrival of her father

questions.question: Select the antonym of the given word. LIBERTY
questions.questionHtml:
Select the antonym of the given word.
LIBERTY
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1.

  • Liberty: the state of being free within society from oppressive restrictions imposed by authority on one's way of life (किसी के जीवन के तरीके पर अधिकार द्वारा लगाए गए दमनकारी प्रतिबंधों से समाज के भीतर मुक्त होने की स्थिति)
  • Dependence: the state of relying on or being controlled by someone or something else; reliance on someone or something for financial support. (किसी पर या किसी और चीज पर निर्भर होने या नियंत्रित होने की अवस्था; वित्तीय सहायता के लिए किसी पर या किसी चीज पर निर्भर रहना)
  • Convenience: the state of being able to proceed with something without difficulty (बिना किसी कठिनाई के कुछ आगे बढ़ने में सक्षम होने की अवस्था)
  • Deliverance: the action of being rescued or set free; a formal or authoritative utterance. (बचाए जाने या मुक्त होने की क्रिया; एक औपचारिक या आधिकारिक उच्चारण)
  • Independence: the fact or state of being independent. (स्वतंत्र होने का तथ्य या अवस्था)

Thus dependence is the antonym of liberty. Other words do not act as antonyms if applied to the context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. BROAD
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

BROAD
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Narrow

Key Points

  • Broad: having a distance larger than usual from side to side; wide; covering a large number and wide scope of subjects.
  • Narrow: of small width in relation to length; limited in extent, amount, or scope.
  • Large: of considerable or relatively great size, extent, or capacity.
  • Wide: of great or more than average width; to the full extent.
  • Long: measuring a great distance from end to end; lasting or taking a great amount of time.

Thus other options are incorrect in the given context. 

Narrow is the antonym of Broad.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Obsolete

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. DEXTERITY
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

DEXTERITY
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 2.

 

  • Let's look at the meaning of the given word and the marked option-
    • Dexterity: Skill in performing tasks, especially with the hands. (कार्यों को करने में निपुणता, विशेषकर हाथों से)
      Example: Reid's dexterity on the guitar.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. DIVIDE
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

DIVIDE
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Unite.

Key Points

The meaning of Divide is to separate or be separated into parts.

So, its antonym must mean something that brings together.

Meanings of the given words:

  • Engulf- powerfully affect (someone); overwhelm.
  • Split- break or cause to break forcibly into parts.
  • Unite- come or bring together for a common purpose or action.
  • Break- separate into pieces as a result of a blow, shock, or strain. 

Out of these, only Unite can give the intended meaning.

questions.question: Select the correct antonym of the given word. Bizarre
questions.questionHtml:
Select the correct antonym of the given word.

Bizarre
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2, i.e., Usual.

Bizarre means very strange or unusual.

So, its opposite meaning word must mean something that is very common.

Meanings of the given words:

Strange- unusual or surprising; difficult to understand or explain.

Usual- habitually or typically occurring or done; customary.

Happy- feeling or showing pleasure or contentment.

Weird- suggesting something supernatural; unearthly.

Out of these, only Usual gives appropriate antonym for Bizarre.

questions.question: Direction : Select the correct antonym of the given word. Allure
questions.questionHtml:
Direction: Select the correct antonym of the given word.

Allure
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Repulse.'
Key Points

  • 'Allure' means powerfully attract or charm; tempt.
    • 'Allure' का अर्थ है शक्तिशाली रूप से आकर्षित या आकर्षण; लुभाना।
      • Example: Will sponsors really be allured by such opportunities?
  • Let us explore the meanings of the given words:
    • Repulse- cause to feel intense distaste and aversion. (तीव्र अरुचि और घृणा महसूस करना।)
    • Attract- cause to come to a place or participate in a venture by offering something of interest or advantage. (किसी स्थान पर आने या किसी उद्यम में रुचि या लाभ की पेशकश करके भाग लेना।)
    • Rewind- to go back, or to make something go back, to an earlier time. (पहले के समय में वापस जाने के लिए, या कुछ वापस करना।)
    • Revive- restore to life or consciousness. (जीवन या चेतना को बहाल करना।)
    • Hence, we can say that the correct antonym of the given word 'Allure' is 'Repulse.'
  • Therefore, the correct answer is 'Repulse.'

Additional Information

  • Let us see the use of the given words in a sentence:
     
Word Sentence
Repulse The enemy attack was quickly repulsed.
Attract These flowers are brightly coloured in order to attract butterflies.
Rewind We can't rewind history and try it a different way.
Revive My plants revived as soon as I gave them some water.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Glee
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Glee
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "Woe". 

Key Points

  • Glee refers to great delight or joy. ("आनंद" or "खुशी".)
    • Example: The child's face was filled with glee when he saw the pile of presents.
  • Woe is the correct antonym, which refers to great sorrow or distress. ("दुःख" or "संताप".)
    • Example: After learning about the tragedy, her heart was filled with woe.
  • Therefore, the correct answer is "Option 1".

Additional Information

  • Bliss is a state of perfect happiness or joy, which is similar in meaning to glee. ("परम सुख" or "आनंद".)
  • Joy refers to a feeling of great pleasure and happiness. ("आनंद" or "खुशी"), making it synonymous with glee.
  • Fun denotes enjoyment, amusement, or light-hearted pleasure. ("मज़ा".)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. FICKLE
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

FICKLE
questions.solution:
The correct antonym is 'Stable'.
Key Points  

  • The word Fickle(adjective) means- likely to change your opinion or your feelings suddenly and without a good reason.​
    • ​Example: The world of popular music is notoriously fickle.
  • ​The antonyms of the word Fickle are- Stable, constant, steady, reliable, aware, etc.
  • The word Stable(adjective) means- firmly fixed or not likely to move or change.
    • ​​Example: She seems more stable these days.
  • Therefore, as per the points mentioned above, we find that the correct answer is option 2).​
  • Let us look at the meanings and examples of the given options:
    • Flighty(adjective)- "not able to keep your attention or interest on one thing for long".
      • ​​Example: She played the part of a flighty, unsuccessful writer.
    • ​Subtle(adjective)- "not loud, bright, noticeable, or obvious in any way".
      • ​​Example: The room was painted a subtle shade of pink.
    • Crafty(adjective)- "clever, especially in a dishonest or secret way".
      • ​​Example: She was a crafty old woman.​

Additional Information

  • The synonyms of the word Fickle are- Capricious, volatile, unsteady, flighty, etc.
  • Example of Fickle in a sentence-
    • Fickle winds made sailing conditions difficult.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Persuade
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Persuade
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. 'Dissuade'

Let's take a look at the table below

Word Meaning
Persuade

Induce (someone) to do something through reasoning or argument(राज़ी करना)

  • Example: It wasn't easy, but I persuaded him to do the right thing. 
Induce

To succeed in persuading or leading (someone) to do something.(प्रेरित)

  • Example: The picks induced many workers to stay away.
Pervade

Spread through and be perceived in every part of (especially of smell)(व्याप्त होना)

  • Example: A smell of stale cabbage pervaded the air.
Dissuade

Persuade (someone) not to take a particular course of action.(मना करना)

  • Example: His friends tried to dissuade him from flying.
Impress

Make (someone) feel admiration and respect(छाप)

  • Example: They immediately impressed the judge.

 

Here we find that the meaning of the word Dissuade is an exact opposite of the word Persuade. Hence the Antonym of the word Persuade is Option 3 Dissuade.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Emerge

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Humane

Humane

  • From the above information, we can say that the word 'construct' is the opposite word for 'demolish.'

Hence, the correct answer is option 3.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. ASCEND
questions.questionHtml:

ASCEND

  • Nefarious (कुटिल): (especially of activities) morally bad (विशेषकर गतिविधियों का) नैतिक रूप से बुरा)
  • Malicious (दुर्भावनापूर्ण): intended to harm or upset other people (अन्य लोगों को नुकसान पहुंचाने या परेशान करने का इरादा है)
  • Malcontent (बाग़ी): a person who is not satisfied with the way things are, and who complains a lot and is unreasonable and difficult to deal with (एक व्यक्ति जो चीजों के तरीके से संतुष्ट नहीं है, और जो बहुत शिकायत करता है और अनुचित और मुश्किल से निपटता है)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. Hazy
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

Hazy
questions.solution:
The correct answer is "clear"
Key Points
  • Hazy (adjective) means
  • "Due to light mist or dust, things are hard to see in hazy weather". (हल्की धुंध या धूल के कारण धुंध के मौसम में चीजें देखना मुश्किल है) 
    • For example, it was a hazy day yesterday.
  • "Uncertain or confused about something". (किसी बात को लेकर अनिश्चित या भ्रमित होना)
    • For example, I have a hazy idea of competitive exams.
  • "Not remembering things clearly". (चीजों को स्पष्ट रूप से याद नहीं रखना) 
    • For example, they were some hazy memories of my childhood.
That's why the antonym of 'Hazy' is 'Clear'.
Additional Information
  • Faint (adjective) means 'feeling weak and getting unconscious'. (कमजोर महसूस करना और बेहोश हो जाना)
  • Soft (adjective) means 'not being hard or firm' (कठोर या दृढ़ नहीं होना)
  • Dim (adjective) means 'not having much light' (ज्यादा रोशनी नहीं होना)
Hence, the correct antonym of 'Hazy' is 'Clear'.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. HASTE
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

HASTE
questions.solution:
Here the correct answer is Delay.

Key Points

  • Let's look at the meaning of the given word:-
    • Haste - excessive speed or urgency of movement or action; hurry. (जल्दी करना; अत्यधिक गति या कार्रवाई की तात्कालिकता)
  • Let's look at the meaning of the correct answer:-
    • Delay - be late or slow; loiter; postpone or defer (an action). (विलंब)
  • Thus, it is clear that the correct antonym of the word 'haste' is 'delay.'
  • Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

  • Let's look at the meaning of the other words given in options:-
    • Urgency - importance requiring swift action. (तात्कालिकता)
    • Drive - operate and control the direction and speed of a motor vehicle. (चलाना)
    • Inspire - fill (someone) with the urge or ability to do or feel something, especially to do something creative. (प्रेरित करना)

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word. GRACEFUL
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate antonym of the given word.

GRACEFUL
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'awkward'.
Key Points
  • Graceful means moving in a smooth, relaxed, attractive way, or having a smooth, attractive shape.
    • She presented herself in a graceful manner.
  • The opposite of this term is awkward which means embarrassed or nervous; moving in a way that is not natural or attractive.
    • No one was expecting such an awkward performance of the singer.
  • Hence, the correct answer is option 4.​
Additional Information
Let's understand the meaning of other words.
  • Attractive - very pleasing in appearance and sound - I still remember one of my classmates who was very attractive.
  • Dangerous - able or likely to cause harm - It is really dangerous to be here at night.
  • Pretty - quite, but not extremely; pleasant to look at - I have got such a pretty daughter.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Constant
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Constant
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'Fluctuating'.
Key Points
  • Constant (adjective) means: 
    • Happening a lot or all the time.
      • John was in constant trouble with his neighbor.
    • Staying the same, not getting less or more.
      • ​The demand for homemade food will always remain constant.
  • The opposite of this term is Fluctuate which means to change or vary frequently between one level or thing and another.
Hence, the correct answer is option 4.
Additional Information Let's understand the meaning of other words.
  • Competent (adjective) - able to do something well - John is competent at his work.
  • Static - staying in one place without moving - Fuel prices have remained static for the last few weeks.
  • Unchanging - not changing, not being different - Some people always say that the habit of drunkards is unchanging.
